text:
Sean Gallagher: kicking off the “incident taxonomy + ownership mapping” reliability initiative. goal is to get to a v1 taxonomy that’s usable during live response + clean enough for reporting. :rotating_light:

Sean Gallagher: scope reminder: Hosted + Dedicated incidents (Private only where we’re primary operator day-2). security stays in Security IR, but we may align on shared metadata fields.

Talia Benson: thanks all. I’ll keep the timeline + deliverables moving. target is ~6-8 weeks end-to-end. I’ll drop a working doc link once it’s cleaned up.

Rafael Mendes: process-wise we need to reduce “who owns this?” confusion during declare + escalation. would like to make category + owner explicit early, but not add a ton of cognitive load.

Miles Thornton: on taxonomy: proposing 2-level structure:
1) Primary incident category (small set, required during incident)
2) contributing factors (multi-select, can be filled in postmortem)
Also: impacted surface (Hosted API / Dedicated / Console / Private / Control Plane / Edge) as required.

Allison Grant: +1. if we keep allowed values tight, we can enforce in dashboards + SLO tooling. if it’s freeform, we’ll never be able to trend.

Priya Natarajan: platform perspective: please keep categories aligned to services (routing/policy/control plane/telemetry). otherwise we’ll keep arguing in every postmortem.

Irene Choi: infra ask: split “capacity exhaustion” from “routing overload” (they present similarly to customers but owners + mitigations differ). also need to separate autoscaling policy issues vs fleet provisioning shortages.

Sean Gallagher: yep. kickoff agenda for today:
- confirm v1 scope + success criteria
- list top incident types we *must* cover
- agree on ownership mapping approach (category-level + service-level)
- timeline + who does what

Sergio Costa: for reporting/dashboards, we need at minimum:
- incident count by category
- TTM/MTTR by category + owner
- breakdown by region + customer tier (hosted vs dedicated)
We can add error budget correlation later.

Aisha Bello: and remediation SLAs. we need a mapping of (sev x category x tier) -> time-to-mitigate + time-to-permanent-fix targets + comm expectations.

Dev Patel: support POV: please ensure categories are understandable by on-call + support. right now tickets get bounced between “infra vs runtime vs routing”. we need a clear “if you see X, page Y” mapping.

Miles Thornton: initial candidate “top types” list from recent pain (not final):
1) Smart routing / policy misconfig (wrong routing decision, degraded mode stuck, fallback loops)
2) Routing overload / request queue blowup (thundering herd, hot shard)
3) Capacity exhaustion (GPU pool full, autoscaling lag, fleet provisioning delay)
4) Runtime crash / OOM (engine segfault, CUDA OOM, kv cache issues)
5) Scheduler regression (batching bug, starvation, latency cliff)
6) Gateway/edge issues (5xx, streaming disconnects, timeouts at edge)
7) Control plane deploy regression (bad config rollout, feature flag)
8) Network / dependencies (cloud provider, DNS, cert, cross-region)
9) Observability/telemetry breakage (alerts missing, dashboards wrong) — question if this is its own category or contributing factor

Allison Grant: I’d keep observability as contributing factor unless the incident is literally “monitoring down” / “paging pipeline broken”. otherwise we’ll dilute categories.

Rafael Mendes: +1. we should keep primary category as “what is broken” not “how we discovered it”. (but we can have “detection gap” as a factor)

Chloe Martin: postmortem template update: I can add required taxonomy fields + a remediation SLA section in the template. but we need the allowed values + definitions first.

Devon Price: on incident-bot: we can add dropdowns for category/impacted surface/tier/region + auto-suggest owner based on category + service. but we should keep required fields minimal on declare.

Sean Gallagher: question to group: should “category” be required at declaration time, or within 15 min?

Rafael Mendes: I’d say required on declare *if* the list is short + definitions are clear. otherwise it slows response.

Dev Patel: support likes required on declare. we need something to route/pull the right SME quickly.

Priya Natarajan: compromise: required on declare but allow “Unknown / needs triage” for first 10 min, then require update. (bot can nag)

Miles Thornton: yep. we can have “TBD” category for live response but only temporarily, and require reclassification in postmortem.

Aisha Bello: as long as dashboards treat “TBD” as an error and we track it. otherwise it’ll become the default.

Sergio Costa: we can enforce “TBD must be resolved within X mins” with a dashboard panel + weekly report.

Talia Benson: timeline proposal:
Week 1-2: inventory last 2-3 quarters, cluster + validate top categories
Week 3-4: finalize taxonomy + ownership mapping + remediation SLA table
Week 5-6: tooling rollout (incident-bot, postmortem template, dashboards)
Week 7: backfill last 90 days + baseline report
(we can compress depending on review cycles)

Sean Gallagher: action items:
- Miles: draft v1 taxonomy list + definitions (aim: <= 12 primary categories)
- Irene + Priya: sanity check boundaries (capacity vs routing vs control plane)
- Allison: draft incident metadata standard fields + allowed values (category, impacted surface, tier, region, contributing factors)
- Aisha: first cut remediation SLA mapping (focus sev1/2 first)
- Devon + Rafael: incident-bot / IC checklist requirements (what’s mandatory when)
- Chloe: postmortem template delta (what fields + where)
- Sergio: dashboard spec (what graphs + data source assumptions)
- Talia: schedule review meeting + track in Linear

Miles Thornton: I’ll post a doc for comments today. request: everyone drop 3-5 “recurring incidents you personally saw” that should influence categories.

Irene Choi: I’ll pull examples:
- dedicated pool saturation (autoscaling lag)
- GPU provisioning delays in us-east-1
- cross-zone network flap causing elevated timeouts

Priya Natarajan: from platform:
- routing policy rollout that increased 429s
- fallback policy loop that hammered a single region
- control plane config push that broke model pinning

Devon Price: quick note on bot implementation: if we add category + impacted service, we can auto-suggest owner + escalation channel. will need a config map maintained somewhere (sheet or yaml).

Allison Grant: for metadata, please decide on canonical list of impacted surfaces. suggest: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (Redwood-operated), Console, Control Plane, Edge/Gateway, Observability.

Rafael Mendes: we should also capture “customer tier” (self-serve vs enterprise, dedicated vs hosted). even if it’s approximate.

Aisha Bello: + “customer comms required?” boolean based on tier + severity. (support wants this)

Dev Patel: yes, and expected cadence (e.g. every 30 min for Sev1 enterprise).

Sean Gallagher: cool. I’m going to pin this thread for now. next step: 30 min working session Thursday to review the taxonomy draft + top 10 incident clusters.

Slackbot APP: Pinned a message to this channel.

Talia Benson: I’ll send calendar + a Linear initiative link once created. please keep comments async in the doc so we can move fast.

Miles Thornton: also: if you have strong opinions about naming, speak now. we need labels that are crisp during incident response (no essays).

Chloe Martin: +1 pls keep categories short enough to fit in a dropdown without wrapping :)

Sean Gallagher: closing note: this is v1. we’re optimizing for adoption + reduced paging ambiguity, not perfect taxonomy. we can iterate once we have data.

Sergio Costa: :thumbsup: once we have the first backfill, I can publish a baseline “top categories + MTTR” slide for monthly review.

Allison Grant: :eyes: watching for any values that overlap with existing severity defs. we should not redefine sev in this effort.

Sean Gallagher: yep. severity stays as-is. taxonomy is orthogonal.

Talia Benson: ok I’ll follow up with docs + meeting invite. thanks everyone.
